office_does: One of the 25th District's two members of the Washington House, voting on state law and the state budgets for a two-year term.
race_blurb: Republican Cyndy Jacobsen, in the House since 2021, faces Democrat Jenn Marie Strickling, a Pierce County charter review commissioner, after a primary decided by under two points. They differ on taxes, public safety and tech regulation.

candidates.summary: State representative since 2021, former Puyallup councilmember, math instructor and accountant, running against new taxes and for police funding and offender accountability.
highlights: Says Washington outspends its revenues and opposes taking 'more of your money' [S1]
Voted against ESSB 6346 and offered amendments to exempt pass-through income and sunset the tax [S4][S6][S7]
Would fund police and pass measures for officer recruitment and retention [S2]

taxes.basis: Stands 'firm against new taxes'; voted against ESSB 6346, ESHB 2081 and ESSB 5814 and sought to narrow or sunset the income tax.

spending.basis: Says the state outspends its revenues every year and calls for budgets that do not take more money.

safety.basis: Prioritizes police funding, recruitment and retention and holding offenders accountable.

experience.basis: In the House since 2021 after three years on the Puyallup City Council, against a first-time legislative candidate.

social.basis: Voted against ESSB 5599; no campaign statement on the topic.

parental-rights.basis: Voted against ESHB 1296's changes to the I-2081 parental-rights list; no campaign statement.

candidates.summary: Pierce County Charter Review Commissioner, small-business owner and former laborers' union member, running on cost of living, labor rights and checks on big tech.
highlights: Wants the wealthiest to 'pay their share' while cutting wasteful spending [S4]
Would ban Flock surveillance cameras and limit corporate data harvesting [S4]
Cites a charter amendment on housing stability and manufactured-home protections [S1][S6]
Endorsed by the WSLC and Planned Parenthood Alliance Advocates [S7][S8]

taxes.basis: Calls the tax code upside-down and wants the wealthiest to pay their share, with relief for working households.

spending.basis: Pairs cutting wasteful spending with full K-12 funding, special education and infrastructure investment.

housing.basis: Cites housing protections to keep seniors and veterans housed and would incentivize affordable and workforce housing.

safety.basis: Pairs police, fire and EMS staffing with community-based crime prevention.

experience.basis: First legislative run after election as a charter review commissioner, against an incumbent in the House since 2021.

local-control.basis: Favors bottom-up local solutions and opposes 'top-down mandates' that ignore rural communities.

tech.basis: Would curb corporate data harvesting, ban Flock cameras, and make data centers pay for the grid costs they impose.

social.basis: Would 'protect reproductive freedom'; endorsed by Planned Parenthood Alliance Advocates.
